.²3 (In <ab>Rhet.</ab>) A figure of speech, ‘Poetical fancy’, which consists in
 supposing {#upameya#} and {#upamAna#} as similar to each other in some

 object under the character of another; {#saMBAvanamaTotprekzA prakftasya#}
 {#pareRa yat#} <ls>K. P. 10</ls>; {%<ab>e. g.</ab>%} {#limpatIva tamo'NgAni varzatIvAYjanaM#}
 {#naBaH#} <ls>Mk. 1. 34</ls>; {#sTitaH pfTivyA iva mAnadaRqaH#} <ls>Ku. 1. 1</ls>. It is usually
 expressed by {#iva#}, or by words like {#manye, SaNke, Druvam, prAyaH#},
 {#nUnam#} <ab>&c.</ab> (see <ls>Kāv. 2. 234</ls>); <ab>cf.</ab> <ls>S. D. 686-692</ls> and <ls>R. G.</ls> under {#utprekzA#} also.
.²4 A parable.
.²5 An ironical comparison.
